artists.biography: It Bites are a rock band formed in Egremont, Cumbria, England, in 1982. Original singer and guitarist Francis Dunnery departed from the band in 1990, to be replaced by Lee Knott (ex-Innocence Lost), who had supported the band on a recent tour at the time. However, in 1991 the band changed its name to Navajo Kiss and then Sister Sarah before splitting in 1992.  It Bites reformed in 2006. Although Dunnery has been replaced by John Mitchell (Kino (UK), Arena, The Urbane, Frost*).  Bassist Dick Nolan was replaced in 2008 with Lee Pomeroy.  The current band members are: John Mitchell (vocals, guitar), John Beck (keyboards), Lee Pomeroy (bass), Bob Dalton (drums)

perplexity.description:
The Big Lad in the Windmill is the debut studio album by British rock band It Bites, released in 1986 on Virgin Records. The album blends progressive rock with pop sensibilities, featuring intricate musicianship, melodic hooks, and dynamic arrangements. Tracks like "Calling All the Heroes" and "Whole New World" showcase the band's ability to merge technical proficiency with accessible songwriting, while the album as a whole reflects the crossover prog style that would become a hallmark of their sound.

As the first release in It Bites' discography, The Big Lad in the Windmill established the group's reputation for blending complex instrumentation with catchy melodies. The album reached No. 35 on the UK Albums Chart and produced three singles, with "Calling All the Heroes" becoming their biggest hit, peaking at No. 6 in the UK. While the album received moderate commercial success and mixed critical reception, it remains a notable entry in the mid-1980s British rock scene for its ambitious fusion of progressive and pop elements.
